A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KaLM-Embedding-V2 research work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, and retained methods and results can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original KaLM benchmark results, model-soup experiments, attention-latency measurements, and a focal-reweighting ablation in Tables 2–9.

after.justification: v3 retains original benchmark results and reports additional V2.5 results, controlled ablations, industrial retrieval evaluations, dimensionality experiments, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed third training stage changes from model-soup parameter averaging to contrastive distillation from Qwen3-Embedding-8B, producing KaLM-Embedding-V2.5. v3 combines contrastive and KL objectives and extends the existing matryoshka training to KL loss. The undistilled V2 variant and its bidirectional Qwen2-0.5B architecture, mean pooling, focal reweighting, and negative mixing remain.

E1.justification: Evaluation expands beyond MTEB to real-user Chinese customer-service FAQ retrieval and game-documentation search in Appendix B. These introduce industrial input conditions and domain-generalization coverage absent from v1. The 31 Chinese and 56 English MTEB tasks and the tabulated training datasets remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The MTEB comparisons retain the earlier baselines and add Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B and, for English, NV-Embed-v2 in Tables 2–4. The new industrial comparison also evaluates Qwen3-Embedding-8B. These are targeted additions within the existing comparison landscape of general-purpose embedding models.

E3.justification: New distillation experiments introduce a one-epoch, approximately 24k-step stage, learning rate 1e-5, KL temperature 0.05, and contrastive/KL weights of 0.3/0.7. Additional protocols include temperature and embedding-dimension sweeps and industrial evaluation using MRR and Recall at 1, 5, and 10. The retained MTEB task selection and original pre-training/fine-tuning budgets remain stable.

E4.justification: v3 retests focal reweighting on V2.5 and adds ablations of negative mixing, bidirectional attention, adding example-based labeling, contrastive versus KL objectives, and temperature. Appendices B–E add industrial generalization tests, dimensionality/MKL ablations, HotpotQA cases, and UMAP analyses. v1's model-soup and inference-latency studies are removed.

E5.justification: v3 adds a fitted logarithmic relationship between baseline model size and performance in Figure 1, plus boxplots summarizing seven hard-negative scores per case in Figure 4. These introduce descriptive statistical summaries, not repeated-run uncertainty. Neither version reports confidence intervals, significance tests, or variability across evaluation runs.

E6.justification: The original V1/V2 benchmark entries, including the full per-dataset tables, are retained. v3 adds the distilled V2.5 variant with Chinese/English MTK scores of 70.93/69.33, alongside retained V2 scores of 68.15/67.47. It also adds industrial, ablation, dimensionality, and qualitative results, while removing the original model-soup, latency, and V2-specific focal-ablation entries.

T1.justification: v3 introduces the mathematical definition of teacher/student similarity distributions and their KL objective in Equation 8. Equation 6 also corrects the mixing-weight normalization from a sum over batch size N to the M hard negatives. Neither version contains theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction redefine the contribution from a single compact model with a model-soup stage to a model series with progressive contrastive distillation. The introduction additionally claims industrial generalization, robustness at reduced embedding dimensions, and improved discrimination and cluster separation. The broad claim of competitive performance below 1B parameters is retained.

C2.justification: v3 introduces substantive interpretations of KL as the primary learning signal, component complementarity, and temperature effects through overly peaked or smoothed teacher distributions. Appendix C distinguishes tasks tolerating small embeddings from retrieval/reranking tasks needing higher dimensions. The earlier explanations of unsuccessful model soup, latency equivalence, and limited exploration under computational constraints disappear.

D1.justification: Appendix A/Table 9 newly document Adam, warm-up settings, teacher-embedding caching, and detailed distillation settings. Section 3.4.1 newly describes 550k persona-based synthetic examples, although their relationship to the unchanged dataset table is unspecified. Conversely, v3 replaces named Ascend 910B/A800 hardware with generic GPU reporting and removes the explicit model/code URLs and MTEB-overlap-filtering statement; these omissions do not establish changed availability or filtering practice.

R1.justification: The related-work framework remains centered on general text embeddings and adapting LLMs. Targeted additions include Hinton's distillation work, Gecko, Persona Hub, and embedding/data-synthesis surveys; model-soup, LM-Cocktail, LoRA, and FlashAttention-2 references are removed. The introduction also places greater emphasis on open, reproducible, commercially usable research.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, contributions become an explicit four-part list, and method explanations gain descriptive subheadings. Experimental settings move from Section 4.1 to Appendix A, while the original appendices become F/G alongside new analysis appendices. Training-data prose is substantially condensed and reorganized, and the author/affiliation block changes.

P2.justification: The original training diagram is expanded into contrastive-learning and distillation workflows. v3 adds a performance overview, a training-stage diagram, case-study boxplots, and UMAP panels. Benchmark tables gain model rows/columns, new analysis and hyperparameter tables appear, and headers, typography, caption placement, and table formatting change throughout.

improvement.justification: v1 offered limited direct validation of several central training choices. v3's Tables 5–8 test those components and compare distillation against additional contrastive training, while Appendices B–C provide evidence about industrial generalization and dimensionality tradeoffs. This substantially strengthens the empirical justification and practical guidance. Removing latency measurements and some reproducibility disclosures is a loss, and repeated-run uncertainty remains absent, but the added controls and documented distillation procedure provide a clear overall quality improvement.
